findings.summary: Imports 'getAvailableAgentTypes' from agent-types.js, but that module does not export it (it imports it from agent-loader.js without re-exporting).
findings.failure_scenario: Module loading fails at import time with 'does not provide an export named getAvailableAgentTypes' because agent-types.ts only exports getValidAgentTypes, not getAvailableAgentTypes. The application cannot start.

findings.summary: Missing 'await' on newly-async createClaudeFlowTools(); iterating the returned Promise with for...of throws TypeError at runtime.
findings.failure_scenario: createClaudeFlowTools returns Promise<MCPTool[]>. The for (const tool of claudeFlowTools) loop tries to iterate a Promise, which has no Symbol.iterator, causing 'TypeError: claudeFlowTools is not iterable' and crashing MCP server startup.

findings.summary: Missing 'await' on newly-async createClaudeFlowTools(); iterating the returned Promise with for...of throws TypeError at runtime.
findings.failure_scenario: Same as server.ts:509. registerClaudeFlowTools() is async but the call lacks await, so claudeFlowTools is a Promise. The for...of on line 426 throws 'TypeError: claudeFlowTools is not iterable', crashing swarm integration startup.

findings.summary: Imports 'VALID_AGENT_TYPES' from agent-types.js, but that export was removed when AGENT_TYPES was replaced with dynamic loading.
findings.failure_scenario: Test file fails to compile/load because VALID_AGENT_TYPES is no longer exported from src/constants/agent-types.ts. All tests in this suite become unrunnable.

findings.summary: Shell injection via execSync with string command constructed from unsanitized arguments that pass through the shell.
findings.failure_scenario: User runs './github-safe.js pr create --title "$(malicious_command)" --body safe'. The title passes through process.argv into the shell command string 'gh pr create --title $(malicious_command) ...'. execSync runs it through /bin/sh, which executes $(malicious_command) as a subcommand.

findings.summary: safeGhCommand passes all options entries to gh CLI, including the internal 'timeout' option, causing gh to fail on an unrecognized --timeout flag.
findings.failure_scenario: Caller passes { timeout: 30000 } in options. The forEach loop on line 33 pushes '--timeout' and '30000' as gh arguments. 'gh issue comment 123 --body-file /tmp/xxx --timeout 30000' fails because gh does not support --timeout.

findings.summary: createIssue writes body to temp file without null/undefined check; a missing body parameter writes the literal string 'undefined'.
findings.failure_scenario: Caller calls gh.createIssue({ title: 'Bug', body: undefined }). The code writes 'undefined' (the string) to the temp file and passes it to gh via --body-file. The GitHub issue body becomes the literal text 'undefined'.

findings.summary: Error from createClaudeFlowCommands() is silently swallowed; users get no indication that slash command creation failed.
findings.failure_scenario: If createClaudeFlowCommands throws (e.g., permission denied on .claude/commands/), the empty catch block discards the error. The user proceeds unaware that their slash commands were not created, leading to missing functionality discovered only when they try to use them.

findings.summary: Error from createClaudeSlashCommands or createOptimizedClaudeSlashCommands is silently swallowed in init flow.
findings.failure_scenario: Same as above but in a different call site within the init command. If slash command creation fails during 'claude-flow init', the user sees a success message but their CLI integrations are missing.
